summary: Laocoön or Lacoon (Ancient Greek: Λαοκόων) of Calydon is an Argonaut, bastard son of King Porthaon by a servant woman and thus half-brother of Oeneus. Aging Oeneus sends him to guard young Meleager on the voyage to Colchis. He is not the Trojan priest of Poseidon.
etymology: Ancient Greek Λαοκόων; Hyginus also spells Lacoon.

sections.heading: Calydonian Argonaut
paragraphs: Apollonius (Argonautica 1.192) and Hyginus (Fabulae 14) list Laocoön among Jason's comrades as Porthaon's son from Calydon. The tradition that Oeneus entrusted Meleager to his half-brother's care during the Colchian voyage keeps him inside the Aetolian royal house.
His myth is catalogue and guardianship, not the serpents-and-wooden-horse drama of the Trojan priest.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id laocoon-calydon is the Argonaut alone. The famous Trojan priest Laocoön (who warns against the horse and is killed with his sons by sea-serpents) is a separate figure; do not merge the two Wikipedia senses under one node.
